newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht seen pressured, ringgit off.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht seen pressured, ringgit off.

text.p: Late European buying of Thai baht forwards after Asian hours on Tuesday pushed up forward rates in the three and six-months and will keep levels high Wednesday, dealers said.
The Thai currency is under pressure due to foreign investors' concern about the export growth Slowdown, political uncertainties and a widening current account deficit.
The gloomy mood was exacerbated by Moody's downgrade of Thai short-term sovereign ceiling ratings for bank deposits and other short-term obligations to Prime 2 from Prime 1.

"The Moody's downgrade sent jitters throughout Europe and we saw selling after hours from a German bank. That's why the forwards today are much higher than where Asia left it," said one dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
On Wednesday, the spot baht rate was steady at 25.309-25.312 to the dollar at 0520 GMT, versus 25.308-25.312 late on Tuesday on dollar's narrow movement abroad, dealers said.
"There was still little buying interest on the U.S. unit today despite the mounting tension in the Gulf," said one currency dealer.
Dealers said the tightening liquidity and high short-term baht interest rates had prompted some dollar selling for the baht in the spot market this morning.
In Indonesia, the rupiah held steady following the release of the trade and inflation data for June and August respectively.
Dealers said trade was relatively quiet despite the figures, which fell within market expectations.
Investors remained wary of central bank intervention over the past few days to defend the lower end of its intervention band, bringing up dollar-rupiah levels, dealers in Singapore said.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,342/2,460 and the conversion rate also by one point to 2,342/2,388 on Tuesday.
The ringgit, meanwhile, extended its fall against the dollar in morning Kuala Lumpur trading as players continued to buy back the U.S. currency to cover short positions, dealers said.
"The market shorted a lot of dollar recently and is now buying back," said one dealer with a foreign bank. "Market position is not favourable for the ringgit at the moment."
